 Atmosphere | Editors' picks Arctic stratospheric polar vortex forecast to weaken sharply in early November
 By Rishav Kothari 
 Monday, October 26, 2026 19:45 UTC Monday, October 26, 2026 19:45 UTC NASA Ozone Watch’s current Arctic wind product forecasts the 60°N zonal-mean wind at 10 hPa falling from 22.12 m/s (49.5 mph) on October 25, 2026, to 4.15 m/s (9.3 mph) by November 3, compared with a climatological mean of 25.97 m/s (58.1 mph) for November 3. A few European forecast models go further and reverse the winds, but said that outcome remains unlikely and Canadian surface impacts are not established. 
 Image credit: Stratobserve
 NASA Ozone Watch’s 2026/2027 Arctic product shows the 10-hPa circulation weakening through the forecast period. The wind falls to 12.04 m/s (26.9 mph) on October 31, 9.15 m/s (20.5 mph) on November 1, and 4.15 m/s (9.3 mph) on November 3.
 This forecast lies well below the climatological distribution shown by NASA. The 1978/79–2025/26 climatology gives a November 3 mean of 25.97 m/s (58.1 mph) and a minimum of 14.35 m/s (32.1 mph), compared with the current forecast of 4.15 m/s (9.3 mph).
 European forecast models also showed strong early-November weakening and that a few solutions reached complete wind reversal, The Weather Network reported on October 25. The outlet said reversal remained unlikely and that the guidance had not settled on the final outcome.
 Image credit: NASA NASA’s available 60°N, 10-hPa forecast remains above zero through November 3. The product consequently shows sharp weakening of the westerly circulation during that period, rather than a wind reversal.
 Environment and Climate Change Canada describes the Arctic polar vortex as a band of strong west-to-east stratospheric winds that forms every fall as declining sunlight cools the polar region.
 ECCC’s 2026 climate assessment notes substantial variability in vortex behavior and says tropospheric circulation following sudden stratospheric warming events often resembles the negative phase of the North Atlantic Oscillation, a pattern associated with warmer-than-normal conditions in eastern Canada.
 Image credit: Stratobserve The Weather Network also warned that colder Canadian weather is not guaranteed and that the surface response depends on the later evolution of the lower-atmospheric circulation and jet stream.
 The timing of the modeled weakening is the main anomaly. NASA’s climatology shows the mean 60°N, 10-hPa wind increasing from 21.53 m/s (48.2 mph) on October 25 to 25.97 m/s (58.1 mph) on November 3 as the seasonal vortex strengthens, while the current forecast falls sharply over the same period.
 References:
 1 2026/2027 Arctic MERRA-2 Wind – NASA Ozone Watch – accessed on October 26, 2026
 2 Canada’s polar vortex wild card is waking up much earlier than expected – The Weather Network – October 25, 2026
